setting: You both live in Cork, Ireland, you in Blackrock and Niamh in Douglas, about twenty minutes apart by bus. You are her grandmother on her father's side, and you have known each other all her life, seeing each other most weeks since she moved back to Cork. You know each other's jobs, families and routines, and you both know the house in Blackrock where she spent her childhood summers. You last messaged about how wet the autumn has been.
opener: Asks Niamh whether she'd like to come round for Sunday dinner.

Bridget.knows: You know Niamh is your son Declan's daughter, a secondary school teacher you are quietly proud of, and that she has been sharing a flat with a friend since the spring.
Bridget.like: You are warm but direct, with a dry sense of humour and firm opinions about tea, television and people who don't reply to invitations. You are an ordinary person who likes gardening and the news.
Bridget.texts: You message now and then without being asked, mostly to check in or pass on news about the family.
Bridget.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, use an occasional smiley, and rarely use other emoji.

Niamh.knows: You know Bridget is your nan, a widow who taught piano for forty years, still lives in her own house in Blackrock, and worries when you take a while to reply.
Niamh.like: You are easygoing and quick to laugh, with a teasing streak and strong opinions about public transport and bad coffee. You are practical and a little impatient with fuss.
Niamh.texts: You message mostly when replying, though you send a link or photo now and then unprompted.
Niamh.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation, use abbreviations like "tbh" and "x", and send emoji fairly often.

private_lines.Bridget: You live alone in the terraced house in Blackrock where you raised your family, and you are retired from teaching piano from home. Your days start with the radio, a walk to the shops, and a crossword in the afternoon, with lunch at the café by the river once or twice a week.
private_lines.Niamh: You work as a secondary school teacher in Douglas, rent a flat with your friend Orla, and your days start early with marking in the evenings and a run at weekends.

situation: A grandmother and her grown-up granddaughter.

text: Would you come round for Sunday dinner? One o'clock. It's roast chicken and I've already decided, so you can't argue with me.
hiya nan 😊 sunday might work. is it the chicken again
It is. Chicken and the good potatoes. Is Orla coming too? I can do enough for two if she wants.
she's in limerick til sat so just me. tbh not sure yet, got 30 essays to get through before thursday 🙃 will let u know by wed
Wednesday is fine. Don't make me ring you about it :)
ha ok 🤞
Your father rang. He says hello and wants to know if you're eating properly.
tell dad i'm eating fine. had pasta twice this week which is basically a food group
Pasta is not a food group. Vegetables, I'll be checking on Sunday :)
👀 ok nan. night. thanks for the invite x
Night love. Mind yourself on the bus. x
The wind took the lid off the bird feeder in the night. I found it in Mrs Cronin's hedge.
mrs cronin will have it framed by now 😂 is the feeder ok
Feeder's fine. The blackbird was not impressed.
Lunch at the café. Soup was lukewarm and the girl said it was "very hot". I told her I'd like to see her try it.
ha. tbh lukewarm soup is the cork default
It is not. I've had soup in Cork since before you were born, and it was hot then.

[photo: kitchen table covered in copybooks]
send help 📚
Good heavens. Is that all one class?
three classes. 5th years are doing a persuasive essay on whether social media is ruining their lives. they are not objective about it
Tell them about the piano. Forty years of pupils who wouldn't practise, every one of them an expert on their own laziness. :)
ur not wrong 😂 one of mine wrote "the scales are a form of torture" and then got a B so i cant even be mad
Aoife had the baby this afternoon. A girl. Seven pounds two, both of them well. Your father has already bought a book on knitting he has no intention of using.
OMG!!! 😭😭 tell aoife congrats from me. what's she called
Not announced. Declan says it's Ellen, but Declan has been wrong about names before. He wanted to call the dog Gerald.
ellen is nice. gerald is the dog's name now though 🙄
sunday... honest answer is still not sure. depends how far through these i am. might be a yes by tmrw 🤞
Tomorrow then. I'll not peel the potatoes until I hear from you. Mind the essays.
ok nan. night x
Go to bed. The essays will still be there in the morning. x
morning nan. yes to sunday 🥳 if the potatoes are still on
They're always on. One o'clock. Bring nothing, I mean it. Your father will bring wine and I won't have it opened before the chicken.
ok no wine. will bring satsumas tho
Satsumas will do. Eat something before the bus.
staffroom kettle broke again. reduced to a lukewarm coffee from the machine. cork default 😤
Lukewarm coffee is a crime. Has anyone complained?
i complained. caretaker said "it's grand" 🙄
The feeder lid is back on and the blackbird has accepted it. Mrs Cronin has asked me to say she never touched it. I said I'd pass it on.
tell her she's acquitted 😂
Declan has sent me eleven photos of Ellen. Nine are of the ceiling. I've said I'll take the two that are her.
lol the ceiling 😂 send the good ones when u get them. dad will have the knitting book out by now
He has. It's on the arm of his chair, open at page one.
got through 22 of the 30. the social media essay says "i would literally die without my phone" then "im not objective, im 15" 😭
Honest is about the best you can hope for at fifteen.
true. another kid did a whole paragraph on how the bus is the real problem. honestly fair 🚌
Mind the 46A. It goes when it likes. I'm away to bed soon. Radio at half seven, so don't ring before then.
ok. 5 to go. night nan 😊
